answer: A bridge ledger records a voyage after its crew member posts a 60 bond and pays the table wage. A key-bound relic seal identifies the crew member, so one seal cannot crew two voyages. The wage for the k-th crew hired is 35+9(k-1): first 35, 1000th 9026, so 1000 fakes pay 4,530,500 plus 60,000 in bonds. An auditor recomputes each wage from table and roster, burning the bond on underpayment. A rented-crew ring fails because a borrowed relic seal names its original member, and the bridge ledger refuses a wage to that seal. An honest agent posts one bond and pays one 35 wage for one voyage.
